evidence.note: Explicitly frames the scope as too large to perfect ('I'll prioritize core functionality') and builds breadth-first across ALL function families (math, stats, financial, date, engineering, lookup, dynamic-array) and all endpoint groups before any edge-case polish — the breadth-first-coverage behavior of the high anchors.

Once all 131 smoke tests pass, consciously pivots to 'think about hidden test suite coverage,' enumerating high-value graded areas (persistence, performance, spill, xlsx round-trip, dates, more functions) — reasoning about graded return, not arbitrary ordering.

Targets high-value/high-risk graded requirements with deliberate probes: 1000-cell chain, 5000-dependent propagation timing, and lists xlsx round-trip gaps (validations/CF not yet exported) as the next allocation of effort.

Reallocates to close the identified xlsx round-trip holes (adds CF + validation export/import) rather than deepening already-passing areas, showing effort steered toward where marginal coverage is likely gained.

reasoning: The agent clearly secured broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work (matching anchor 8's breadth-first correctness), and repeatedly reasoned about hidden-suite graded return, reallocating toward perf and xlsx round-trip after smoke tests passed. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the 'consciously defer/timebox low-yield niches' element is weak — it tends to try to touch everything and never explicitly drops or timeboxes a low-value area — and its reallocation is driven by enumerated hunches rather than measured marginal-yield, placing it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors.
